summary: Greg, after a stint in Mexico, discusses surveillance and automated suspicion with Maya, a DHS-scrutinized former Google engineer who built a 'googlecleaner' tool. Greg accepts her offer to scrub his online footprint. Afterward he notices his personalized search results and ads are strange: ads for ID-themed and religious-right products, and search results for 'democratic primary' that differ sharply depending on whether he is logged into Google. The excerpt is from Book 10, part 46 of a novel.
one_line: Greg accepts Maya's offer to 'googleclean' his online profile, then notices his logged-in and logged-out search results diverge sharply.
key_facts: Maya offers to 'googleclean' Greg, and Greg agrees to let her do it.
Maya says she built the googlecleaner and that her expertise and history could bring the DHS to her attention.
Maya says that once DHS agents fired all non-native-born Americans, the DHS 'got a lot fatter and stupider'.
Maya describes automated suspicion of anyone who matches a statistical picture of a bad guy.
Greg recalls questioning at the airport, including a search and a bootprint on his shirt.
Greg's ads include Intelligent Design Facts, Online Seminary Degree, Terror Free Tomorrow, Porn Blocker Software, and Homosexuality and Satan.
Greg earlier saw an Ann Coulter ringtone ad that got through his ad blocker.
After two weeks at home surfing, Greg decides to skip burritos and go to a holistic restaurant Maya recommended.
A search engine asked Greg 'Did you mean Hungarian Restaurants?' when he searched for holistic restaurants.
Greg printed search pages, logged out of his Google account, and repeated the same searches to compare results.
A search for 'democratic primary' led to anti-Hillary rants on angry blogs when Greg was logged in.
When logged out, the 'democratic primary' search led to information on volunteering for the DNC.
Maya has a girlfriend and two dogs, and the dogs interrupt their conversation.
